=== crosshatch (46 lines) ===
# Crosshatch ink

![sample](sample.png)

A sketchy ink line that boils on 2s, crosshatch and coloured-pencil shading clipped inside shapes, stipple, paper grain. Warm cream paper and wood by day; navy "inside the computer" worlds with periwinkle lines and glowing accents.

## Palette

`C` in `kit/core.js`. Day: ink `#3a2417`, paper `#f4ecd9`, cream `#efe5cf`, wood `#d6a466`, yellow `#f0c55a`, green `#5f9c5c`, red `#d4382c`, sky `#9cc4d6`, rose `#d98b8b`. Night: navy `#0c0d1c` / `#15173a`, periwinkle `#c8d0f0`, cyan `#52d6c4`, magenta `#e0368f`, glow green `#5de37a`. **Terracotta `#d97757` is the hero** (the ink dot); red pencil dashes `rgba(212,56,44,0.92)` mean a plan.

## The medium


=== cut-paper (45 lines) ===
# Cut paper

![sample](sample.png)

Torn-edge paper shapes with soft drop shadows, paper grain and crayon in the fills, patterns (stripes, dots, gingham, wood grain), full-bleed colour worlds, and characters with simple faces. Collage-style animation: playful, warm, busy with small life.

## Palette

`PAL` in `kit.js`. Warm and saturated, on cream: ink `#2a1d18`, paper `#fbf6ea`, cream `#f3ead6`, navy `#26315f`, wood `#c08048`, mustard `#d9a441`, yellow `#f6cf55`, teal `#3f9f9a`, mint `#a9d9c6`, pink `#f3a3bf`, sky `#cfe2ee`, purple `#8c7ad8`, blue `#4c6fb5`, green `#5aa05a`, skin tones, charcoal. **Orange `#ec7a4f` is reserved for the spark** (the hero) — never decoration.

## The medium


=== isometric (95 lines) ===
# Isometric line art

![sample](sample.png)

Calm, precise product illustration: objects in 2:1 dimetric isometric on a white ground, drawn only with constant hairlines. Grey silhouettes and edges, lighter inner and receding lines, faces filled white so nearer objects hide farther lines. Rounded slabs and plates with visible thickness, stacked layers, grids of repeated parts (keys, vents, pillars, ports), and one tiny dark accent per frame. Motion on 1s with spring settles; otherwise still. Studied from MIT-licensed isometric line figures (references kept local, never copied).

## Measured (from the reference figures' live SVG, and screenshots of them)

| what | reference | this style |
|---|---|---|
| ground | `#ffffff` (screenshot palette: the 248 bucket, 95-99% of pixels) | `#ffffff`; 97% of a frame |
| silhouette / edges | `rgb(164,164,172)`, 0.9px non-scaling | `#a4a4ac` (= 164,164,172), **2.0px at 1080 wide** |

=== math (159 lines) ===
# Math

![sample](sample.png)

A manim-style math explainer look. Coloured math on a near-black stage:
- serif type that is **Written** on
- axes, number planes and graphs that **ShowCreation** sweeps draw
- equations and shapes that **Transform** into each other
- a tracking dot with a live decimal readout
- a small pi-shaped hero with eyes that watches the math happen

The motion is smooth, on 1s, and eased with manim's sigmoid `smooth`. Nothing boils and there's no texture or grain. It's clean vector strokes, so the colour coding does the work.

=== pixel (90 lines) ===
# Pixel

![sample](sample.png)

Pixel art. Every picture is drawn at a low internal resolution — 90x160, 135x240, 180x320 for a 9:16 frame — with whole-pixel primitives in a limited palette, then scaled up nearest-neighbour to 1080x1920. Hard square pixels, ordered (Bayer) dithering instead of gradients, a built-in 5x7 bitmap font, sprites from string arrays, and screen effects that belong to a device: an LCD grid for a handheld, scanlines and a curved-tube vignette for an arcade. **Resolution can tell time:** an early era is chunkier than a later one, so a chronology gets sharper as it goes.

## Resolutions per era

Each era picks an internal resolution that divides 1080x1920 exactly, so every pixel is a whole square on screen. Declare it in `src/bridges.js` as `ERA_RES = [[w, h], ...]`; scenes draw with `lowres(ERA_RES[e], ...)`, and the STYLE hooks read it to size morph windows, the morphing blob and the post effects.

| res | pixel size | feels like | glyphs across (5x7 font) |
|---|---|---|---|

=== riso (92 lines) ===
# Riso

![sample](sample.png)

A three-ink risograph print on cream paper: halftone screens at their own angles, overprints instead of mixed colours, plates a few pixels off register, ink dropouts that sparkle in the darks. Flat, bright, a little worn, on 2s.

**The one rule: nothing is painted, everything is printed.** A frame is a sheet of paper run through three spot-ink plates. A plate only says how much ink goes where (a grey tone 0..1). The screen turns that tone into dots at the plate's angle, and the inks multiply. There is no black ink and no white ink.

The parameters below were measured from a reference print animation (1080 wide, 24fps, 120 BPM) and then rebuilt in code; the demo here is an original subject.

## Palette


=== sketchbook (79 lines) ===
# Sketchbook

![sample](sample.png)

Graphite and one accent colour on a warm sketchbook page. Every line is drawn by hand and boils on 2s. Things get **pencilled in, inked over, then coloured with a quick scribble**, and hand lettering on the page does the narrating. The page is the world: its dot grid, spiral binding, smudges and coffee ring stay in view, and the camera moves across the page instead of cutting away from it.

## Palette (`SK` in kit.js)

| role | value | use |
|---|---|---|
| paper | `#f2ead8` | the page; also the blank sheet a morph happens on |
| ink | `#2a2420` | settled lines, lettering, eyes |

Selesai. 7 style dari `animate` di-port ke `motion/style/`:

1. `crosshatch` (sketchy ink boiling on 2s, hatch/pencil/stipple, navy/cream)
2. `cut-paper` (torn paper, drop shadows, crayon, spark hero)
3. `isometric` (2:1 dimetric product line art, hairlines, spring settles)
4. `math` (manim blackboard, axes, formulas, smooth easing)
5. `pixel` (retro pixel art, dither, scanlines, 16-color palette)
6. `riso` (3-ink risograph print, halftone screens, misregistration)
7. `sketchbook` (graphite pencil + accent on dot-grid paper, hand lettering)

Struktur per style (`style/<name>/`):
- `style.json` → metadata + canvas (1080×1920, 30fps) + engines (`remotion`, `fframes`)
- `docs/` → `style-guide.md`, `style-prompt.md`, `sample.png`
- `remotion/` → `kit/` (tokens, kit, overlays, transitions, fonts), `template/`, `sync_kit.sh`
- `fframes/` → `Cargo.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `src/` (lib, tokens, kit, look, video, main), `template/`, `tools/ff.sh`

Fixes:
- Bug path `$L/style` di `core/new_episode.sh` → fix ke `$MOTION_LIB/style`.

<skill-invocation name="motion-qa">
# Papercut QA

Compare stills for style, not content, against the Style DNA and the storyboard. Run it per scene while building and once on the whole reel before the final render.

## Preflight

- Install: **Standard** or Full. Stills need a scaffolded project with Remotion, and the contact sheets need Python with numpy and Pillow (`$MOTION_PY`). Missing pieces: `./install.sh --doctor`, then `motion-setup`.
- Library: `$MOTION_LIB`, else the `MOTION_LIB=` line in `~/.config/motion-explainer/config.env`, else ask once.
- Read first: Style DNA in `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md` section 2, and the backdrop sheet `style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/public/bg/backdrops/_sheet.jpg`. Each image costs about 0.7-1.5k tokens, so open only what the step needs.
- For density, `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/frame-breakdown.md` ("Pacing stats" at the end): scenes average 2.8 s, 2-4 discrete visual events per scene, one every 0.4-0.8 s on a stressed word, a new caption page about every 0.6 s. Copy the density, not the content.

## 1. Render stills

From the project's `video/` folder:

```
$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/qa.sh NAME FROM-TO NTH [SCALE=0.3] [COLS=9]
```

- Use 4-6 timestamps per check. For a scene, NTH is about its length in frames divided by 4. Leave `FROM-TO` out for the whole reel and raise NTH.
- The output is `out/qa/NAME_0.jpg` (and `_1`, `_2` for longer ranges), at most 45 frames per sheet. Read the sheet; keep sheets small.
- One QA command per scene, and never two renders at once. Keep fixes to two rounds per scene.
- Check against the storyboard: the scene's frame 0, its key events on their words, nothing clipped, nothing covering the banner or caption bands.

## 2. Checklist

- [ ] Every object reads as paper: grain, rough edge, drop shadow, stacked-piece shading, no outlines or gradients.
- [ ] The world camera moves smoothly. Only the banner and labels boil (stepped, subtle).
- [ ] The banner is fixed in position and taped, 3-7 words, one fact each, never repeats the VO. The banners alone read as a fact sheet.
- [ ] Every set illustrates a concrete word in its VO line, numbers are physical props, and there is one callback set before the CTA.
- [ ] Every number and UI label traces to the facts list. The script has at least one honest limitation and a feature stack of exactly three.
- [ ] Captions: one tag per word, tilted, popping on onset, pages of 1-3, in the 68-80% band, never on a face.
- [ ] Saturation only on characters, captions and signals.
- [ ] A visual event on every stressed word, with ambient motion always running.
- [ ] Cuts on banner changes (sets 1.5-3 s in tours and news, up to 5 s in a metaphor beat), bottom 20% clear.
- [ ] **The HOOK block (SAY / WRITE / SHOW / ALIGN) is on screen exactly as written:** frame 0 shows the SHOW moment mid-action with the WRITE title on it, and the first VO line is SAY.
- [ ] Every scene has a camera move, at most one page turn or tear, a tape pull or whip into the CTA, and every transition has its SFX.
- [ ] Humour pass visible on screen: one format throughout, a costume prop per idea, one struggling beat, the frame-0 prop returns changed in the CTA set, and every gag reads in under 1 s and never covers the banner, the captions or the key number.
- [ ] Vocabulary in the VO and banners matches the audience level in `SERIES.md`.
- [ ] Voiceover, captions and events are in sync (scrub the Studio at every cut).

For a failed item, fix the scene file (or the kit in the library, never `src/lib/` in the project) and re-run the one scene. Rebuild a scene with `motion-build`.

## 3. Deliver

Open the Studio preview, list the scenes with timings, and say what is placeholder: voice, music, SFX, assets. If the voice is a placeholder, say how to re-voice it (`motion-voice`). After posting, the numbers go to `motion-strategy` for the autopsy.

## Principles pass

Scrub one scene at 5 fps and check against `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/motion-principles.md`: anticipation before each big move (2), everything eased (6), something trailing after impacts (5), one focal prop (3), one exaggerated beat (10), stacked shading and a consistent shadow (11).

## Hand-off

Fixes go back to `motion-build` (scene or sound) or `motion-voice` (sync). A clean pass ends the reel: render with `$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/render.sh` when the user asks.
</skill-invocation>
</system-reminder>

<skill-invocation name="motion-explainer">
# Papercut Explainer

A ~20-45 s vertical explainer that looks like layered construction paper brought to life: grainy paper props with drop shadows, rigid cut-out animation, a slow camera push with stop-motion paper boil, a taped headline banner per beat and word-by-word torn-paper caption tags. Built with Remotion, optional AI-generated textured assets, and any TTS.

Every beat runs three tracks:
- the voiceover tells the story
- the taped banner adds a hard fact the voiceover skips
- a fresh paper set illustrates the voiceover's words, with a rough papercut rebuild of the product UI doing the demo

Reuse the style and the storytelling, not the worked examples' content. Every product, company and number in the examples is invented. The style rules are in `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md` (section 2 is the Style DNA).

## Preflight

- **Library.** Resolve `$MOTION_LIB`, else the `MOTION_LIB=` line in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env`, else ask once. Never hard-code a machine path. Stages 1 to 4 need no library.
- **Install mode.** Probe it before promising a stage (see Install modes below).
- **Series.** Find the series folder (it holds `episodes/`). Read its `SERIES.md` if it exists.

## Run modes (ask first)

1. **Full reel**, idea to mp4: stages 1 to 8, then stage 9 after posting.
2. **Script only**: strategy, hook, script (stop after the staging table).
3. **Storyboard from an existing script**: `motion-storyboard`. Ask for the script, the facts and the HOOK block.
4. **Style prompt for another tool**: give the right block from `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-prompt.md` and stop.
5. **Fix or rebuild one scene**: `motion-build` (scenes step), then `motion-qa`.

## Intake (ask only what is missing)

- **Source**: usually a link (repo, product site, announcement). Everything else is researched from it.
- **The one claim** the video proves, and the topic.
- **Role framing**: who or what does the work, who advises or approves. Confirm it with the user and never invent product behaviour.
- **CTA keyword** and what the viewer gets (the deliverable).
- **Length**: default 22-30 s.
- **Audience level** (from `SERIES.md`) and any accent colour or mascot.

Write the answers as the BRIEF block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` (format in `motion-strategy`).

## Stages

| # | Stage | Skill | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Strategy | `motion-strategy` | `SERIES.md`, the source | BRIEF in `research/facts.md`, `SERIES.md` |
| 2 | Hook | `motion-hook` | BRIEF | HOOK block at the top of `video/STORYBOARD.md` |
| 3 | Script | `motion-script` | BRIEF, HOOK | `research/facts.md`, `narration/script.json`, staging table in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 4 | Storyboard | `motion-storyboard` | `script.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | Camera/Cut table, scene blocks, SFX plan in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 5 | Scaffold and plan | `motion-build` | `STORYBOARD.md` | the project, `episode.json` |
| 6 | Voice and timing | `motion-voice` | `script.json`, `voice/voice.json` | `narration/` takes, `public/vo/captions.json`, `src/plan.json` |
| 7 | Scenes, sound, render | `motion-build` | `plan.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | `src/scenes/*`, `tools/cues.json`, `out/*.mp4` |
| 8 | QA | `motion-qa` | stills, `STORYBOARD.md` | fixes, the delivery summary |
| 9 | After posting | `motion-strategy` (autopsy), `motion-build` (harvest) | platform numbers, the project | `research/analytics/`, library promotions |

## Project files

The pipeline lives in files, not in chat. Each stage reads the files above and writes its own, so a new session can resume from any stage.

```
<series>/
  SERIES.md                  optional: audience, voice, palette, mascot, keyword log
  voice/voice.json           optional: voice settings (copy library/voice/voice.example.json)
  video-assets/           optional: overlay textures and props
  research/analytics/        optional: competitor studies and autopsies
  episodes/NN-slug/
    research/facts.md        BRIEF + facts with sources
    narration/script.json    [{"id": "l1_hook", "text": "..."}, ...]
    video/
      episode.json           scenes, banners, hook, gaps, bed, cuts
      STORYBOARD.md          HOOK, staging table, Camera/Cut table, scene blocks
```

Library catalogs: `style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/CATALOG.md` (every kit component) and `$MOTION_LIB/core/audio/CATALOG.md` (every SFX and bed). They are generated, so a fresh checkout may lack them or have stale ones. Run `python3 $MOTION_LIB/core/tools/catalog.py` to rebuild. Agents read the catalogs, not the kit source.

Reuse before writing: a kit component, a props set or a scene template beats new drawing code. Pick SFX and beds by name.

## Install modes

- **Minimal** (skills only): strategy, hook, script, storyboard, style prompts. No rendering.
- **Standard**: Minimal + build and render with a placeholder voice (silent, or macOS `say`) via `$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/placeholder_vo.py`, stills QA, SFX and bed audio, the full mp4.
- **Full**: Standard + local Qwen3-TTS voiceover and word-timed captions from real audio.

Probe (read-only):

```
. "$(grep '^MOTION_LIB=' "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env" | cut -d= -f2-)/env.sh"   # fills MOTION_PY, QWEN_TTS_PY
node -v; ffmpeg -version | head -1
"$MOTION_PY" -c 'import numpy, PIL, soundfile'
"$QWEN_TTS_PY" -c 'import qwen_tts'
```

The first three lines passing means Standard. The `qwen_tts` import passing as well means Full. If a stage needs more than the install provides, say so in one line, run `./install.sh --doctor` from the repo root, and hand over to `motion-setup` instead of improvising. Find the root with `readlink` on the installed skill folder (under `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.config/opencode/skills` or another harness's skills folder), or `MOTION_HOME` in the config file.

## Rules across stages

- Strategy notes win over style notes: 22-30 s, and no news-framed hooks.
- Parallelise independent work (scene groups, backdrops and props, re-renders) with agents in one go.
- Render only when asked. Preview in the Remotion Studio.

## Shared references

- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md`: Style DNA, drawing in papercut, palette, fonts, texture, camera and jitter, motion timings, captions, sound.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-prompt.md`: portable prompts for other agents and generators.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/motion-principles.md`: the 12 principles of animation mapped to kit components and helpers, with a use-in-each-stage note.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/RECIPES.md`: Remotion component sketches, for when there is no library.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/asset-prompts.md`: what to generate versus build in code, with prompt templates.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/frame-breakdown.md`: a worked ~28 s example at 0.2 s resolution. Copy its event density, not its content.

## Hand-off

Start at stage 1 for a full reel, or at the stage the run mode names. After intake, run `motion-strategy`; it reads `SERIES.md` and the BRIEF and hands to `motion-hook`. Each stage skill names the next one.
</skill-invocation>

<skill-invocation name="motion-hook">
Reference files (use Read when needed):
  - /mnt/shared/Project/Other/motion/skills/motion-hook/references/hook-patterns.md

# Papercut hook

The hook is the most important step. A reel's hook is three separate, explicit layers, and none may be skipped or left implied. Write all of them before anything else in the script.

## Preflight

- Install: Minimal is enough. No library needed.
- Read the BRIEF at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` (topic, format, audience, CTA) and the facts list, so every claim can be checked. If there is no BRIEF, run `motion-strategy` first.
- Read `SERIES.md` for the audience level and regions.

## The HOOK block

```
HOOK
SAY:   <the first spoken sentence>
WRITE: <the frame-0 title, 2-5 words, ideally a number; the episode.json "hook">
SHOW:  <what frame 0 and the first 2 s show: the mid-action moment, the camera move>
ALIGN: <the one idea all three point at>
```

No scene gets built until all four lines are filled and pass the alignment test.

| Layer | Rule |
|---|---|
| SHOW, the first frame | The most striking moment, already mid-action. No establishing shot, no fade-in, no empty room. It must make sense muted. |
| WRITE, the on-screen title | The cover title (2-5 words, ideally a number), fully visible on frame 0 for about 2-3 s. It carries the other half of the gap, never the same words as the voice. |
| SAY, the spoken line | Opens the gap within about 10 words. Names who it's for. The stake or number comes early. Never answers itself. No anonymous news framing ("Someone just released..."); a named, credible source is fine. |

Skip the "stated as news" opening from beat 1 of the spine ("A solo dev just open-sourced..."). Open the gap and the stake instead, and name a big brand the viewer already knows in the first sentence.

## Alignment test

What you show, what you write and what you say all point at one idea. They differ in words, never in subject. If the voice says "your screenshots leaked" while frame 0 is a calm desk and the title is about stars, each layer opens a different loop and none lands. Cover any two layers: the remaining one should still hint at the same idea.

## Variants and the hook check

1. Write 5 variants from at least three of the seven patterns in `references/hook-patterns.md` (borrowed authority + giveaway, name the viewer then a number, one object one number one twist, price shock, pain, verdict or conflict, own authority).
2. Score each with one point per yes:
   1. Does the spoken line open a gap (a question or tension the viewer needs closed) within about 10 words?
   2. Does it say who it's for, or what is at stake?
   3. Does it carry one concrete number, object or twist instead of a vague claim?
   4. Does it leave the answer for later?
   5. Does frame 0 plus the title work with the sound off?
   6. Is every claim true to the facts sheet?
3. Pick the variant with the most points. Drop any variant that fails question 6.

## The frame-0 title (`episode.json` "hook")

Every reel opens on its hook. The `hook` key in `episode.json` puts the cover title on screen from frame 0 (`build_vo.py` writes it into `plan.json`) and holds the banner back until the title leaves.

```
"hook": {"lines": [["AI", "LEAKED"], ["13,000+"]], "hot": ["13,000+"], "until": "yes", "size": 108, "top": 220}
```

- `lines`: the WRITE text as torn tags, one array of words per line. `hot`: the words that get the yellow tag.
- The title leaves at the onset of the `until` word (`["yes", 2]` for its 2nd occurrence), or after `"hold"` seconds (default 2.4).
- Title stays 2-5 words and shares no words with SAY.

## The cut out of the hook carries motion

A hook that ends on a held pose feels abrupt and drops the attention it just earned.
- Give the hook scene's last ~10 frames an accelerating push (a tiny pull back first).
- Scene 2 opens on an impact at its focal prop, then the camera eases back to the set. For example, the proof card slams onto the board with a `stamp`, the camera starts at 1.17x, and a character scurries in from off-frame.
- End the title on the cut with `"hook": {"hold": <S01 seconds>}` so it lifts away during the push instead of covering scene 2's first frames.

## Gate

- [ ] SHOW is mid-action on frame 0 and reads muted.
- [ ] WRITE is on frame 0 and isn't the spoken words.
- [ ] SAY opens the gap within 10 words.
- [ ] All three pass the alignment test, and ALIGN names the one idea.
- [ ] The winning variant scored best and passed question 6.

## Hand-off

Write the HOOK block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/video/STORYBOARD.md` (create the file if it isn't there). Note the hook's key word or number; the script's last line repeats it. Next is `motion-script`, which also puts SAY into line `l1_hook` of `narration/script.json`.
</skill-invocation>

content.text:
# Bang Motion **An agent skill that turns your AI coding agent into a motion designer.**
Openers, promos, product demos, kinetic typography, and explainers — built as a single `index.html` that plays like video, not like slides. [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.19.0-2f6fd6?style=flat-square)](CHANGELOG.md) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-3fa34d?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/format-Agent%20Skills-1c2a4a?style=flat-square)](#install) [![Works with](https://img.shields.io/badge/works%20with-Claude%20Code%20%C2%B7%20Codex%20%C2%B7%20Gemini%20CLI%20%C2%B7%20Cursor-7a5af5?style=flat-square)](#install) [What you can make](#what-you-can-make) · [Style gallery](#style-gallery) · [Workflow](#recommended-workflow) · [Example prompts](#example-prompts) · [Install](#install) · [FAQ](#faq)
--- ## Why Ask an AI agent for "a video" and you usually get **slides**: one section per idea, a title, a photo, a fade between them. Bang Motion encodes what a working motion designer insists on — one continuous world, a camera that actually moves, a subject that persists, text that lives inside the scene — as **rules an agent can check in its own code**, plus starters that make the right architecture the easy path. It also stops every project from looking the same. The look is **derived from your brand** through a required style brief, the structure is **chosen from a menu of concepts**, and nothing is inherited from the starter or copied from a reference. ## What you can make | | Output | Typical length | |---|---|---| | 🎬 **Openers & promos** | product launches, app promos, campaign spots, teasers | 15–40 s | | 🖥️ **Product & SaaS demos** | UI assembled and used on screen, camera following the clicks | 20–60 s | | 🔤 **Kinetic typography** | lyric-style statements, event announcements, manifestos | 10–30 s | | 📺 **Bumpers, idents, channel intros** | short brand moments that loop | 3–10 s | | 🧭 **Explainers** | six explainer styles, optional voice-over sync, 16:9 or 9:16 | 30–120 s | | 🎥 **Video layers** | your own or generated clips placed like footage — inside devices, frames, and masks, locked to the timeline | — | | 🎞️ **After Effects builds** | cartoon explainers built directly inside AE through the Higgsfield MCP bridge | — | Every deliverable is one `index.html`: double-click to play, autoplay + loop, `?debug=1` for a scrub bar, and an optional frame-by-frame export to MP4. ## Style gallery > Each frame below is a **single static scene** built for this README with **fictional brands and data**. The portrait, product photos, port photo, engraving, and cartoon cutouts were generated with GPT Image 2.5; everything else is HTML, CSS, and SVG. Real projects take their palette, type, and imagery from your brand. === docs/ === gallery === references/ === ae-bridge-higgsfield.md anti-ppt.md architecture.md explainer.md kartun-panggung.md opener-konsep.md roadmap.md techniques.md

Grainy gradient · opener
Glowing layered shapes, soft grain, a camera that travels through them. Tech, AI, music, premium launches.
Poster color-block · kinetic typography
Huge cropped words, solid color fields that slam in on the beat. Events, music, launches.

Product tour with claims · SaaS demo
Real UI lifted out of the dashboard, the camera zooms into what gets clicked. SaaS, dashboards, B2B.
Flat vector illustration · promo
Solid fills, stylized hands, UI drawn flat, shapes with gentle overshoot. Fintech, consumer apps.

Flat pop with photos · promo
Photo cutouts popping in, stickers, brand color fields that change with a visible trigger. Consumer apps, campaigns.
Continuous action · explainer
One subject that never stops, numbers and maps living inside the world. Speed, routes, processes.

Kapan berganti: kapan pun dibutuhkan, direncanakan di style brief — mood
atau topik segmen berubah (masalah → solusi, klaim → produk, isi → CTA),
brand warna-warni menuntut ritme warna (medan warna palet bergantian), atau
aksi di layar mengubahnya (toggle dinyalakan, benda menutup lensa, ikon
membesar memenuhi frame). Bumper pendek atau opener satu mood boleh satu
warna latar, tetapi latar itu tetap BERGERAK (§7c) — latar diam ditolak.
Yang tidak sah: latar yang tidak pernah dipertimbangkan (gelap otomatis
karena starter-nya gelap) dan pergantian tanpa pemicu. Bila berganti: di
titik cut/ketukan, di balik wipe/benda (camThrough/wipe/leak), atau sebagai
akibat aksi di layar — tidak pernah cross-fade tanpa sebab; teks ganti
varian (`.ink`) dan kantong gelap (`.pocket`) dimatikan di adegan terang;
vignette diringankan (0,3–0,4), bloom WebGL dimatikan. Gradien terang
contoh: `background:linear-gradient(160deg,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent-lit) 30%,#fff),#fff 55%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 14%,#fff))`.

## 7c. Menu gerak latar — "gerak tiap detik" bukan berarti benda melintas

Kegagalan yang umum: opener untuk produk berbeda sama-sama memakai
batang/potongan cahaya yang melesat ke samping, karena aturan "gerak harus
ada di dunia (objek melintas) tiap detik" dibaca sempit — model memilih cara
termurah lalu mencari alasannya dari produk. Gerak latar dipilih di style brief dari
menu ini, dan harus berbeda dari proyek sebelumnya:

| # | Bahasa gerak latar | Rasa | Catatan |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Latar bertekstur + kamera bernapas + satu gerak halus (tint/cahaya/grain bergeser pelan) | tenang, mahal | pilihan paling tenang yang masih sah; latar yang benar-benar diam ditolak |
| 2 | Gradien besar yang berpindah/berputar pelan (2–3 warna palet) | lembut, modern | `background-position`/sudut di-tween 8–15 dtk |
| 3 | Blob warna mengambang (2–4 lingkaran blur) | ramah, ringan | ikut palet; drift ±60 px, 4–6 dtk |
| 4 | Grain/tekstur kertas yang hidup (offset mask per frame dari t) | organik, cetak | jangan noise acak — offset dari `t` |
| 5 | Sapuan cahaya SEKALI per segmen (light sweep) | premium | bukan sapuan terus-menerus |
| 6 | Bentuk geometris besar (lingkaran/garis/logo negatif) berputar 20–40 dtk per putaran, 2 lapis parallax | brand, kuat | bentuk dari logo/tema |
| 7 | Partikel NAIK pelan (debu, gelembung, percik) | hangat, hidup | bukan horizontal; opacity ≤ .35 di kantong teks |
| 8 | Grid/pola yang bernapas (skala/opacity 1.0↔1.04, 6–10 dtk) | teknis, presisi | tanpa scroll |
| 9 | Teks hantu raksasa bergeser lambat di belakang | editorial | kontras rendah ≥ .12, satu gaya |
| 10 | Foto/ilustrasi tema dengan Ken Burns + parallax 2 lapis | naratif | butuh gradasi gelap di sisi teks |
| 11 | Aliran horizontal (streak/lane/range/hujan partikel) | kecepatan, data | HANYA bila tema = kecepatan/aliran; sudah dipakai dua proyek berturut → hindari kecuali dengan cara yang jelas baru |
| 12 | Medan warna palet bergantian (sapuan/snap 0,15–0,3 dtk, dipicu benda, aksi UI, atau ketukan) | pop, energik | untuk brand warna-warni; tiap medan diisi bentuk flat/objek yang bergerak |

Aturan: satu bahasa per opener (boleh dua bila latar berganti antar
segmen), ditulis di style brief pada baris "gerak latar", terpisah dari
"tanda tangan gerak" (yang menggerakkan OBJEK/teks, bukan latar). Menu ini
juga berlaku untuk latar WebGL §7: nebula yang berdrift pelan + kamera bernapas
adalah #1, debu naik adalah #7; "tunnel/rush" adalah #11. Latar tidak pernah
diam di adegan mana pun; pergantian warna latar (§7b) boleh ditambahkan di atas
bahasa gerak mana pun.

## 7d. Menu permukaan latar — gradien, cahaya, tekstur (jangan flat)

"Gelap ≤ 25 % / terang ≥ 80 % di bawah teks" adalah aturan KANTONG TEKS,
bukan perintah membuat seluruh latar flat satu warna. Opener yang diterima
memakai latar yang kaya: gelap dengan glow radial di horizon, terang dengan
gradien lembut dan blob warna palet. Menu (semua dari token palet; nilai
bebas diubah):

```css
/* a. glow horizon (gelap) */ background:radial-gradient(70% 42% at 50% 108%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 34%,transparent),color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 12%,transparent) 48%,transparent 70%),linear-gradient(180deg,#05060a,var(--base) 60%,#0b1020);
/* b. duotone diagonal   */ background:linear-gradient(160deg,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 55%,#000) 0%,var(--base) 45%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent-lit) 30%,#000) 100%);
/* c. mesh terang (blob) */ background:#F7FAFF; + 3–4 <i> radial-gradient(circle,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent-lit) 38%,#fff),transparent 66%) berukuran 800–1200 px, drift ±60 px
/* d. spotlight + tint   */ background:radial-gradient(55% 60% at 50% 40%,color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 18%,var(--base)),var(--base) 75%);
/* e. langit berlapis    */ background:linear-gradient(180deg,#cfe0f5 0%,#f5efe3 100%); + pita warna tipis 2–3 lapis dengan opacity .2–.4
/* f. tekstur + tint     */ kertas/grain (feTurbulence) di atas a/b/c dengan mix-blend-mode:multiply/overlay, opacity .1–.3
/* g. grainy gradient    */ gradien jenuh 2–3 warna di BENTUK dan latar + lapisan butiran halus di atas semuanya (resep di bawah)
```
Aturan: flat satu warna hanya untuk arah "poster color-block" (diberi
grain/tekstur halus) dan "flat pop berfoto" (medan flat sah karena berganti
cepat dan selalu diisi bentuk flat/objek yang bergerak). Setiap latar punya ≥ 2 lapis (dasar + cahaya/
tekstur/blob). Warna latar dari palet tema, bukan hitam/putih murni.

content.text:
# Anti-PPT — hukum desain adegan

Dokumen ini adalah alasan skill ini ada: hasil yang "secara teknis benar" tetap
gagal bila terasa seperti presentasi PPT.

## Kenapa model selalu jatuh ke pola slide

Model dilatih menyusun INFORMASI: judul → penjelas → bukti pendukung.
Struktur itu bagus untuk dokumen, dan fatal untuk motion graphic.
Video promosi tidak menjelaskan — ia **menyatakan**, satu pukulan per shot,
dan membiarkan gerakan + musik yang membawa emosinya. Kalau kamu merasa
sebuah adegan "kurang informasi", itu justru tanda adegannya sudah benar.

## Tabel pelanggaran → perbaikan

| Pelanggaran | Perbaikan |
|---|---|
| Kicker "02 — FITUR" + judul 2 baris + body copy 2 baris + 4 chip badge, layout kolom kiri-kanan | Satu kalimat ≤ 5 kata di tengah-atas + satu objek produk naik ke tengah |
| Tiga baris teks besar berisi tiga klaim "TANPA …" | Headline 2 kata + satu cara dari menu fitur (`opener-konsep.md`): satu fitur didemokan, kata berganti, objek bertransformasi, kartu dikocok, grid tile… — dipilih per proyek |
| Opener produk B memakai kulit opener produk A (palet, glow, nebula, font yang sama) karena diambil dari starter/proyek lama | Gaya diturunkan dari brand B lewat style brief: palet dari logo/ikon B, font berkarakter lain, bahasa latar lain, tanda tangan gerak lain (SKILL.md Hukum #3) |
| Semua judul KAPITAL SEMUA, font lebar bobot 800, selalu di tengah, masuk dengan stagger huruf yang sama — terasa kaku | Sentence case bobot 500, penekanan pada kata kunci (sorotan kata opsional — bisa juga kata per kata, ukuran, jeda, objek di samping kata), tanpa titik otomatis (tanda baca hanya bila mengubah arti), ukuran/arah/posisi bergantian (techniques.md §1) |
| Setiap judul/klaim diakhiri titik, termasuk frase dua kata — terasa kaku dan seperti template | Default tanpa titik; `?` untuk pertanyaan sungguhan, titik hanya untuk gaya dua kalimat pendek yang disengaja dan konsisten (techniques.md §1 aturan 5) |

rem_template = os.path.join(sdir, "remotion", "template")

os.makedirs(docs_dir, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(rem_kit, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(rem_kit, "ui"), exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(os.path.join(rem_template, "src", "scenes"), exist_ok=True)

os.makedirs(os.path.join(ff_template, "media"), exist_ok=True)

# 1. Copy sample image
src_sample = os.path.join(BANG_DIR, "docs", "gallery", "01-grainy-gradient.jpg")
if os.path.exists(src_sample):
    shutil.copy2(src_sample, os.path.join(docs_dir, "sample.png"))
    shutil.copy2(src_sample, os.path.join(sdir, "sample.png"))
elif os.path.exists(os.path.join(BANG_DIR, "icon.png")):
    shutil.copy2(os.path.join(BANG_DIR, "icon.png"), os.path.join(docs_dir, "sample.png"))
    shutil.copy2(os.path.join(BANG_DIR, "icon.png"), os.path.join(sdir, "sample.png"))

# 2. style.json
cfg = {
    "name": "bang-motion",
    "title": "Bang Motion",
    "tagline": "Cinematic promo and explainer motion graphics: glowing horizon backgrounds, living grain, continuous camera drift, and anti-PPT pacing.",
    "description": "High-end motion design style ported from bang-motion. Multi-layer glowing horizon backgrounds, soft film grain, glassmorphic UI cards, kinetic editorial typography, and motivated 3D push-through transitions.",
    "canvas": {
        "width": 1080,
        "height": 1920,
        "fps": 30,
        "bannerZone": [0.12, 0.20],
        "captionsBand": [0.68, 0.80],
        "keepClearBottom": 0.80
    },
    "engines": ["remotion", "fframes"],
    "audio": {
        "sfx": "../../core/audio/sfx",
        "beds": "../../core/audio/beds"
    },
    "docs": {
        "styleGuide": "docs/style-guide.md",
        "stylePrompt": "docs/style-prompt.md"
    },
    "enginesDoc": {
        "remotion": "remotion/README.md",
        "fframes": "fframes/README.md"
    }
}
with open(os.path.join(sdir, "style.json"), "w") as f:
    json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)

# 3. docs/style-guide.md
guide = """# Bang Motion Style Guide

![sample](sample.png)

High-end cinematic motion graphics for product demos, openers, kinetic typography, and explainers. Designed to defeat the "PPT/slides" trap:
1. **One continuous world:** Never static slides. The background breathes and drifts.
2. **Rich multi-layer background:** Dark deep base (#07090e) transitioning to a glowing horizon (#38bdf8 / #6366f1) + animated floating blobs + fine living film grain.
3. **Kinetic editorial typography:** Sentence case headlines with crisp contrast, drop shadows, and motivated focus highlights.
4. **Floating glass UI:** Translucent cards with frosted glass backdrop blur, hairline borders, and spotlight sweeps.
5. **Camera breathing:** Subtle continuous camera drift (scale 1.0 -> 1.05) on 1s with smooth ease curves.
"""
with open(os.path.join(docs_dir, "style-guide.md"), "w") as f:
    f.write(guide)

with open(os.path.join(docs_dir, "style-prompt.md"), "w") as f:
    f.write(f"# Style Prompt: Bang Motion\n\n{cfg['tagline']}\n\n{cfg['description']}\n")

# 4. sync_kit.sh
sync_sh = f"""#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
rp() {{ python3 -c 'import os,sys;print(os.path.realpath(sys.argv[1]))' "$1"; }}
if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then echo "usage: $0 <project dir> [assets dir]" >&2; exit 2; fi
L=$(dirname "$(rp "${{BASH_SOURCE[0]}}")"); P=$(rp "$1")
mkdir -p "$P/src/lib" "$P/public/bg" "$P/public/assets" "$P/public/fonts"
rsync -a --delete "$L/kit/" "$P/src/lib/"
printf '%s\\n' "synced from {STYLE}/kit on $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'); do not edit here, edit the library and re-sync" > "$P/src/lib/SYNCED.txt"
if [ -d "$L/public/fonts" ]; then rsync -a "$L/public/fonts/" "$P/public/fonts/"; fi
if [ -d "$L/public/bg" ]; then rsync -a "$L/public/bg/" "$P/public/bg/"; fi
if [ -n "${{2:-}}" ]; then rsync -a "$(rp "$2")/" "$P/public/"; fi
echo "{STYLE} kit -> $P/src/lib ($(find "$P/src/lib" -name '*.ts*' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') files)"
"""
sync_p = os.path.join(sdir, "remotion", "sync_kit.sh")
with open(sync_p, "w") as f:
    f.write(sync_sh)
os.chmod(sync_p, 0o755)

# 5. tools/ff.sh
ff_sh = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
exec "${CARGO:-cargo}" run --release -- "$@"
"""
ff_p = os.path.join(ff_tools, "ff.sh")
with open(ff_p, "w") as f:
    f.write(ff_sh)
os.chmod(ff_p, 0o755)

# 6. rust-toolchain.toml
toolchain = """[toolchain]
channel = "1.91.0"
components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]
"""
with open(os.path.join(sdir, "fframes", "rust-toolchain.toml"), "w") as f:
    f.write(toolchain)
with open(os.path.join(ff_template, "rust-toolchain.toml"), "w") as f:
    f.write(toolchain)

print("Base scaffolding for bang-motion complete.")

Style `bang-motion` selesai dibuat di `style/bang-motion` untuk **remotion** dan **fframes**.

DNA visual:
- Anti-PPT: dunia kontinu, kamera bernapas, bukan slide statis.
- Multi-layer background: `GlowHorizon` (gradient hitam malam `#07090e` ke horizon bawah menyala `#38bdf8`), `GrainyMeshBlob`, living micro-film grain.
- UI & typography: `GlassCard` (frosted glass, backdrop blur, hairline border), `KineticTitle` (editorial high-contrast sentence case), `StatusPill`.

Struktur package (`style/bang-motion/`):
- `style.json` → canvas 1080×1920 @ 30fps, engines: `remotion`, `fframes`
- `docs/` → `style-guide.md`, `style-prompt.md`, `sample.png`
- `remotion/` → `kit/` (tokens, kit, overlays, transitions, fonts), `template/`, `sync_kit.sh`
- `fframes/` → `Cargo.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `src/` (lib, tokens, kit, look, video, main), `template/`, `tools/ff.sh`

Verifikasi:
```bash
. /mnt/shared/Project/Other/motion/core/env.sh
motion_styles
# Output:
# bang-motion
# crosshatch
# cut-paper
# isometric
# math
# papercut
# pixel
# riso
# sketchbook
```

./core/new_episode.sh <series_dir> 01-intro Episode my-video --style bang-motion --engine remotion

```

<system-reminder>
<skill-invocation name="motion-qa">
# Papercut QA

Compare stills for style, not content, against the Style DNA and the storyboard. Run it per scene while building and once on the whole reel before the final render.

## Preflight

- Install: **Standard** or Full. Stills need a scaffolded project with Remotion, and the contact sheets need Python with numpy and Pillow (`$MOTION_PY`). Missing pieces: `./install.sh --doctor`, then `motion-setup`.
- Library: `$MOTION_LIB`, else the `MOTION_LIB=` line in `~/.config/motion-explainer/config.env`, else ask once.
- Read first: Style DNA in `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md` section 2, and the backdrop sheet `style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/public/bg/backdrops/_sheet.jpg`. Each image costs about 0.7-1.5k tokens, so open only what the step needs.
- For density, `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/frame-breakdown.md` ("Pacing stats" at the end): scenes average 2.8 s, 2-4 discrete visual events per scene, one every 0.4-0.8 s on a stressed word, a new caption page about every 0.6 s. Copy the density, not the content.

## 1. Render stills

From the project's `video/` folder:

```
$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/qa.sh NAME FROM-TO NTH [SCALE=0.3] [COLS=9]
```

- Use 4-6 timestamps per check. For a scene, NTH is about its length in frames divided by 4. Leave `FROM-TO` out for the whole reel and raise NTH.
- The output is `out/qa/NAME_0.jpg` (and `_1`, `_2` for longer ranges), at most 45 frames per sheet. Read the sheet; keep sheets small.
- One QA command per scene, and never two renders at once. Keep fixes to two rounds per scene.
- Check against the storyboard: the scene's frame 0, its key events on their words, nothing clipped, nothing covering the banner or caption bands.

## 2. Checklist

- [ ] Every object reads as paper: grain, rough edge, drop shadow, stacked-piece shading, no outlines or gradients.
- [ ] The world camera moves smoothly. Only the banner and labels boil (stepped, subtle).
- [ ] The banner is fixed in position and taped, 3-7 words, one fact each, never repeats the VO. The banners alone read as a fact sheet.
- [ ] Every set illustrates a concrete word in its VO line, numbers are physical props, and there is one callback set before the CTA.
- [ ] Every number and UI label traces to the facts list. The script has at least one honest limitation and a feature stack of exactly three.
- [ ] Captions: one tag per word, tilted, popping on onset, pages of 1-3, in the 68-80% band, never on a face.
- [ ] Saturation only on characters, captions and signals.
- [ ] A visual event on every stressed word, with ambient motion always running.
- [ ] Cuts on banner changes (sets 1.5-3 s in tours and news, up to 5 s in a metaphor beat), bottom 20% clear.
- [ ] **The HOOK block (SAY / WRITE / SHOW / ALIGN) is on screen exactly as written:** frame 0 shows the SHOW moment mid-action with the WRITE title on it, and the first VO line is SAY.
- [ ] Every scene has a camera move, at most one page turn or tear, a tape pull or whip into the CTA, and every transition has its SFX.
- [ ] Humour pass visible on screen: one format throughout, a costume prop per idea, one struggling beat, the frame-0 prop returns changed in the CTA set, and every gag reads in under 1 s and never covers the banner, the captions or the key number.
- [ ] Vocabulary in the VO and banners matches the audience level in `SERIES.md`.
- [ ] Voiceover, captions and events are in sync (scrub the Studio at every cut).

For a failed item, fix the scene file (or the kit in the library, never `src/lib/` in the project) and re-run the one scene. Rebuild a scene with `motion-build`.

## 3. Deliver

Open the Studio preview, list the scenes with timings, and say what is placeholder: voice, music, SFX, assets. If the voice is a placeholder, say how to re-voice it (`motion-voice`). After posting, the numbers go to `motion-strategy` for the autopsy.

## Principles pass

Scrub one scene at 5 fps and check against `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/motion-principles.md`: anticipation before each big move (2), everything eased (6), something trailing after impacts (5), one focal prop (3), one exaggerated beat (10), stacked shading and a consistent shadow (11).

## Hand-off

Fixes go back to `motion-build` (scene or sound) or `motion-voice` (sync). A clean pass ends the reel: render with `$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/render.sh` when the user asks.
</skill-invocation>
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
<skill-invocation name="motion-explainer">
# Papercut Explainer

A ~20-45 s vertical explainer that looks like layered construction paper brought to life: grainy paper props with drop shadows, rigid cut-out animation, a slow camera push with stop-motion paper boil, a taped headline banner per beat and word-by-word torn-paper caption tags. Built with Remotion, optional AI-generated textured assets, and any TTS.

Every beat runs three tracks:
- the voiceover tells the story
- the taped banner adds a hard fact the voiceover skips
- a fresh paper set illustrates the voiceover's words, with a rough papercut rebuild of the product UI doing the demo

Reuse the style and the storytelling, not the worked examples' content. Every product, company and number in the examples is invented. The style rules are in `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md` (section 2 is the Style DNA).

## Preflight

- **Library.** Resolve `$MOTION_LIB`, else the `MOTION_LIB=` line in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env`, else ask once. Never hard-code a machine path. Stages 1 to 4 need no library.
- **Install mode.** Probe it before promising a stage (see Install modes below).
- **Series.** Find the series folder (it holds `episodes/`). Read its `SERIES.md` if it exists.

## Run modes (ask first)

1. **Full reel**, idea to mp4: stages 1 to 8, then stage 9 after posting.
2. **Script only**: strategy, hook, script (stop after the staging table).
3. **Storyboard from an existing script**: `motion-storyboard`. Ask for the script, the facts and the HOOK block.
4. **Style prompt for another tool**: give the right block from `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-prompt.md` and stop.
5. **Fix or rebuild one scene**: `motion-build` (scenes step), then `motion-qa`.

## Intake (ask only what is missing)

- **Source**: usually a link (repo, product site, announcement). Everything else is researched from it.
- **The one claim** the video proves, and the topic.
- **Role framing**: who or what does the work, who advises or approves. Confirm it with the user and never invent product behaviour.
- **CTA keyword** and what the viewer gets (the deliverable).
- **Length**: default 22-30 s.
- **Audience level** (from `SERIES.md`) and any accent colour or mascot.

Write the answers as the BRIEF block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` (format in `motion-strategy`).

## Stages

| # | Stage | Skill | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Strategy | `motion-strategy` | `SERIES.md`, the source | BRIEF in `research/facts.md`, `SERIES.md` |
| 2 | Hook | `motion-hook` | BRIEF | HOOK block at the top of `video/STORYBOARD.md` |
| 3 | Script | `motion-script` | BRIEF, HOOK | `research/facts.md`, `narration/script.json`, staging table in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 4 | Storyboard | `motion-storyboard` | `script.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | Camera/Cut table, scene blocks, SFX plan in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 5 | Scaffold and plan | `motion-build` | `STORYBOARD.md` | the project, `episode.json` |
| 6 | Voice and timing | `motion-voice` | `script.json`, `voice/voice.json` | `narration/` takes, `public/vo/captions.json`, `src/plan.json` |
| 7 | Scenes, sound, render | `motion-build` | `plan.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | `src/scenes/*`, `tools/cues.json`, `out/*.mp4` |
| 8 | QA | `motion-qa` | stills, `STORYBOARD.md` | fixes, the delivery summary |
| 9 | After posting | `motion-strategy` (autopsy), `motion-build` (harvest) | platform numbers, the project | `research/analytics/`, library promotions |

## Project files

The pipeline lives in files, not in chat. Each stage reads the files above and writes its own, so a new session can resume from any stage.

```
<series>/
  SERIES.md                  optional: audience, voice, palette, mascot, keyword log
  voice/voice.json           optional: voice settings (copy library/voice/voice.example.json)
  video-assets/           optional: overlay textures and props
  research/analytics/        optional: competitor studies and autopsies
  episodes/NN-slug/
    research/facts.md        BRIEF + facts with sources
    narration/script.json    [{"id": "l1_hook", "text": "..."}, ...]
    video/
      episode.json           scenes, banners, hook, gaps, bed, cuts
      STORYBOARD.md          HOOK, staging table, Camera/Cut table, scene blocks
```

Library catalogs: `style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/CATALOG.md` (every kit component) and `$MOTION_LIB/core/audio/CATALOG.md` (every SFX and bed). They are generated, so a fresh checkout may lack them or have stale ones. Run `python3 $MOTION_LIB/core/tools/catalog.py` to rebuild. Agents read the catalogs, not the kit source.

Reuse before writing: a kit component, a props set or a scene template beats new drawing code. Pick SFX and beds by name.

## Install modes

- **Minimal** (skills only): strategy, hook, script, storyboard, style prompts. No rendering.
- **Standard**: Minimal + build and render with a placeholder voice (silent, or macOS `say`) via `$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/placeholder_vo.py`, stills QA, SFX and bed audio, the full mp4.
- **Full**: Standard + local Qwen3-TTS voiceover and word-timed captions from real audio.

Probe (read-only):

```
. "$(grep '^MOTION_LIB=' "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env" | cut -d= -f2-)/env.sh"   # fills MOTION_PY, QWEN_TTS_PY
node -v; ffmpeg -version | head -1
"$MOTION_PY" -c 'import numpy, PIL, soundfile'
"$QWEN_TTS_PY" -c 'import qwen_tts'
```

The first three lines passing means Standard. The `qwen_tts` import passing as well means Full. If a stage needs more than the install provides, say so in one line, run `./install.sh --doctor` from the repo root, and hand over to `motion-setup` instead of improvising. Find the root with `readlink` on the installed skill folder (under `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.config/opencode/skills` or another harness's skills folder), or `MOTION_HOME` in the config file.

## Rules across stages

- Strategy notes win over style notes: 22-30 s, and no news-framed hooks.
- Parallelise independent work (scene groups, backdrops and props, re-renders) with agents in one go.
- Render only when asked. Preview in the Remotion Studio.

## Shared references

- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md`: Style DNA, drawing in papercut, palette, fonts, texture, camera and jitter, motion timings, captions, sound.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-prompt.md`: portable prompts for other agents and generators.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/motion-principles.md`: the 12 principles of animation mapped to kit components and helpers, with a use-in-each-stage note.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/RECIPES.md`: Remotion component sketches, for when there is no library.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/asset-prompts.md`: what to generate versus build in code, with prompt templates.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/frame-breakdown.md`: a worked ~28 s example at 0.2 s resolution. Copy its event density, not its content.

## Hand-off

Start at stage 1 for a full reel, or at the stage the run mode names. After intake, run `motion-strategy`; it reads `SERIES.md` and the BRIEF and hands to `motion-hook`. Each stage skill names the next one.
</skill-invocation>
</system-reminder>

<skill-invocation name="motion-qa">
# Papercut QA

Compare stills for style, not content, against the Style DNA and the storyboard. Run it per scene while building and once on the whole reel before the final render.

## Preflight

- Install: **Standard** or Full. Stills need a scaffolded project with Remotion, and the contact sheets need Python with numpy and Pillow (`$MOTION_PY`). Missing pieces: `./install.sh --doctor`, then `motion-setup`.
- Library: `$MOTION_LIB`, else the `MOTION_LIB=` line in `~/.config/motion-explainer/config.env`, else ask once.
- Read first: Style DNA in `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md` section 2, and the backdrop sheet `style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/public/bg/backdrops/_sheet.jpg`. Each image costs about 0.7-1.5k tokens, so open only what the step needs.
- For density, `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/frame-breakdown.md` ("Pacing stats" at the end): scenes average 2.8 s, 2-4 discrete visual events per scene, one every 0.4-0.8 s on a stressed word, a new caption page about every 0.6 s. Copy the density, not the content.

## 1. Render stills

From the project's `video/` folder:

```
$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/qa.sh NAME FROM-TO NTH [SCALE=0.3] [COLS=9]
```

- Use 4-6 timestamps per check. For a scene, NTH is about its length in frames divided by 4. Leave `FROM-TO` out for the whole reel and raise NTH.
- The output is `out/qa/NAME_0.jpg` (and `_1`, `_2` for longer ranges), at most 45 frames per sheet. Read the sheet; keep sheets small.
- One QA command per scene, and never two renders at once. Keep fixes to two rounds per scene.
- Check against the storyboard: the scene's frame 0, its key events on their words, nothing clipped, nothing covering the banner or caption bands.

## 2. Checklist

- [ ] Every object reads as paper: grain, rough edge, drop shadow, stacked-piece shading, no outlines or gradients.
- [ ] The world camera moves smoothly. Only the banner and labels boil (stepped, subtle).
- [ ] The banner is fixed in position and taped, 3-7 words, one fact each, never repeats the VO. The banners alone read as a fact sheet.
- [ ] Every set illustrates a concrete word in its VO line, numbers are physical props, and there is one callback set before the CTA.
- [ ] Every number and UI label traces to the facts list. The script has at least one honest limitation and a feature stack of exactly three.
- [ ] Captions: one tag per word, tilted, popping on onset, pages of 1-3, in the 68-80% band, never on a face.
- [ ] Saturation only on characters, captions and signals.
- [ ] A visual event on every stressed word, with ambient motion always running.
- [ ] Cuts on banner changes (sets 1.5-3 s in tours and news, up to 5 s in a metaphor beat), bottom 20% clear.
- [ ] **The HOOK block (SAY / WRITE / SHOW / ALIGN) is on screen exactly as written:** frame 0 shows the SHOW moment mid-action with the WRITE title on it, and the first VO line is SAY.
- [ ] Every scene has a camera move, at most one page turn or tear, a tape pull or whip into the CTA, and every transition has its SFX.
- [ ] Humour pass visible on screen: one format throughout, a costume prop per idea, one struggling beat, the frame-0 prop returns changed in the CTA set, and every gag reads in under 1 s and never covers the banner, the captions or the key number.
- [ ] Vocabulary in the VO and banners matches the audience level in `SERIES.md`.
- [ ] Voiceover, captions and events are in sync (scrub the Studio at every cut).

For a failed item, fix the scene file (or the kit in the library, never `src/lib/` in the project) and re-run the one scene. Rebuild a scene with `motion-build`.

## 3. Deliver

Open the Studio preview, list the scenes with timings, and say what is placeholder: voice, music, SFX, assets. If the voice is a placeholder, say how to re-voice it (`motion-voice`). After posting, the numbers go to `motion-strategy` for the autopsy.

## Principles pass

Scrub one scene at 5 fps and check against `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/motion-principles.md`: anticipation before each big move (2), everything eased (6), something trailing after impacts (5), one focal prop (3), one exaggerated beat (10), stacked shading and a consistent shadow (11).

## Hand-off

Fixes go back to `motion-build` (scene or sound) or `motion-voice` (sync). A clean pass ends the reel: render with `$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/render.sh` when the user asks.
</skill-invocation>
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
<skill-invocation name="motion-explainer">
# Papercut Explainer

A ~20-45 s vertical explainer that looks like layered construction paper brought to life: grainy paper props with drop shadows, rigid cut-out animation, a slow camera push with stop-motion paper boil, a taped headline banner per beat and word-by-word torn-paper caption tags. Built with Remotion, optional AI-generated textured assets, and any TTS.

Every beat runs three tracks:
- the voiceover tells the story
- the taped banner adds a hard fact the voiceover skips
- a fresh paper set illustrates the voiceover's words, with a rough papercut rebuild of the product UI doing the demo

Reuse the style and the storytelling, not the worked examples' content. Every product, company and number in the examples is invented. The style rules are in `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md` (section 2 is the Style DNA).

## Preflight

- **Library.** Resolve `$MOTION_LIB`, else the `MOTION_LIB=` line in `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env`, else ask once. Never hard-code a machine path. Stages 1 to 4 need no library.
- **Install mode.** Probe it before promising a stage (see Install modes below).
- **Series.** Find the series folder (it holds `episodes/`). Read its `SERIES.md` if it exists.

## Run modes (ask first)

1. **Full reel**, idea to mp4: stages 1 to 8, then stage 9 after posting.
2. **Script only**: strategy, hook, script (stop after the staging table).
3. **Storyboard from an existing script**: `motion-storyboard`. Ask for the script, the facts and the HOOK block.
4. **Style prompt for another tool**: give the right block from `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-prompt.md` and stop.
5. **Fix or rebuild one scene**: `motion-build` (scenes step), then `motion-qa`.

## Intake (ask only what is missing)

- **Source**: usually a link (repo, product site, announcement). Everything else is researched from it.
- **The one claim** the video proves, and the topic.
- **Role framing**: who or what does the work, who advises or approves. Confirm it with the user and never invent product behaviour.
- **CTA keyword** and what the viewer gets (the deliverable).
- **Length**: default 22-30 s.
- **Audience level** (from `SERIES.md`) and any accent colour or mascot.

Write the answers as the BRIEF block at the top of `episodes/NN-slug/research/facts.md` (format in `motion-strategy`).

## Stages

| # | Stage | Skill | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Strategy | `motion-strategy` | `SERIES.md`, the source | BRIEF in `research/facts.md`, `SERIES.md` |
| 2 | Hook | `motion-hook` | BRIEF | HOOK block at the top of `video/STORYBOARD.md` |
| 3 | Script | `motion-script` | BRIEF, HOOK | `research/facts.md`, `narration/script.json`, staging table in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 4 | Storyboard | `motion-storyboard` | `script.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | Camera/Cut table, scene blocks, SFX plan in `STORYBOARD.md` |
| 5 | Scaffold and plan | `motion-build` | `STORYBOARD.md` | the project, `episode.json` |
| 6 | Voice and timing | `motion-voice` | `script.json`, `voice/voice.json` | `narration/` takes, `public/vo/captions.json`, `src/plan.json` |
| 7 | Scenes, sound, render | `motion-build` | `plan.json`, `STORYBOARD.md` | `src/scenes/*`, `tools/cues.json`, `out/*.mp4` |
| 8 | QA | `motion-qa` | stills, `STORYBOARD.md` | fixes, the delivery summary |
| 9 | After posting | `motion-strategy` (autopsy), `motion-build` (harvest) | platform numbers, the project | `research/analytics/`, library promotions |

## Project files

The pipeline lives in files, not in chat. Each stage reads the files above and writes its own, so a new session can resume from any stage.

```
<series>/
  SERIES.md                  optional: audience, voice, palette, mascot, keyword log
  voice/voice.json           optional: voice settings (copy library/voice/voice.example.json)
  video-assets/           optional: overlay textures and props
  research/analytics/        optional: competitor studies and autopsies
  episodes/NN-slug/
    research/facts.md        BRIEF + facts with sources
    narration/script.json    [{"id": "l1_hook", "text": "..."}, ...]
    video/
      episode.json           scenes, banners, hook, gaps, bed, cuts
      STORYBOARD.md          HOOK, staging table, Camera/Cut table, scene blocks
```

Library catalogs: `style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/CATALOG.md` (every kit component) and `$MOTION_LIB/core/audio/CATALOG.md` (every SFX and bed). They are generated, so a fresh checkout may lack them or have stale ones. Run `python3 $MOTION_LIB/core/tools/catalog.py` to rebuild. Agents read the catalogs, not the kit source.

Reuse before writing: a kit component, a props set or a scene template beats new drawing code. Pick SFX and beds by name.

## Install modes

- **Minimal** (skills only): strategy, hook, script, storyboard, style prompts. No rendering.
- **Standard**: Minimal + build and render with a placeholder voice (silent, or macOS `say`) via `$MOTION_LIB/core/tools/placeholder_vo.py`, stills QA, SFX and bed audio, the full mp4.
- **Full**: Standard + local Qwen3-TTS voiceover and word-timed captions from real audio.

Probe (read-only):

```
. "$(grep '^MOTION_LIB=' "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/motion-explainer/config.env" | cut -d= -f2-)/env.sh"   # fills MOTION_PY, QWEN_TTS_PY
node -v; ffmpeg -version | head -1
"$MOTION_PY" -c 'import numpy, PIL, soundfile'
"$QWEN_TTS_PY" -c 'import qwen_tts'
```

The first three lines passing means Standard. The `qwen_tts` import passing as well means Full. If a stage needs more than the install provides, say so in one line, run `./install.sh --doctor` from the repo root, and hand over to `motion-setup` instead of improvising. Find the root with `readlink` on the installed skill folder (under `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.config/opencode/skills` or another harness's skills folder), or `MOTION_HOME` in the config file.

## Rules across stages

- Strategy notes win over style notes: 22-30 s, and no news-framed hooks.
- Parallelise independent work (scene groups, backdrops and props, re-renders) with agents in one go.
- Render only when asked. Preview in the Remotion Studio.

## Shared references

- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-guide.md`: Style DNA, drawing in papercut, palette, fonts, texture, camera and jitter, motion timings, captions, sound.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/style-prompt.md`: portable prompts for other agents and generators.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/motion-principles.md`: the 12 principles of animation mapped to kit components and helpers, with a use-in-each-stage note.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/remotion/RECIPES.md`: Remotion component sketches, for when there is no library.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/asset-prompts.md`: what to generate versus build in code, with prompt templates.
- `$MOTION_LIB/style/$MOTION_STYLE/docs/frame-breakdown.md`: a worked ~28 s example at 0.2 s resolution. Copy its event density, not its content.

## Hand-off

Start at stage 1 for a full reel, or at the stage the run mode names. After intake, run `motion-strategy`; it reads `SERIES.md` and the BRIEF and hands to `motion-hook`. Each stage skill names the next one.

[**🇺🇸 EN**](README.en.md) · [🇨🇳 简中](README.zh-CN.md) · [🇯🇵 日本語](README.ja.md) · [🇰🇷 한국어](README.ko.md) · [🇫🇷 FR](README.fr.md) · [🇧🇷 PT-BR](README.pt-BR.md) · [🇹🇷 TR](README.tr.md) · [🇮🇩 ID](README.id.md) # 🎬 Stickman Video Director **Turn any script into viral, multi-style animated stickman videos for Faceless YouTube Channels.** [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/kaomei/stickman-video-director?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director/stargazers) ![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-16a34a?style=flat-square) Start with a topic, an article, or a script. Automatically orchestrate visuals, voiceovers, captions, and sound effects into a production-ready stickman video. **⚡ 100% Free & Open-Source. No camera, no $50/mo subscriptions, and ready in minutes, not days.** Continually updated visual styles for **science explainers, dark psychology, tech parables, viral lore, and storytelling channels.**
=== line-art-animation === # line-art-animation A Claude skill and a small TypeScript library for animated line-art components: ink-on-paper figures that walk, ride and react, in scenes that run from day to night. Everything is drawn live in SVG, so it stays sharp at any size and responds to the pointer. ![A Japanese street drawn in line art, going from late afternoon to night](media/village.gif) | Day | Night | |---|---| | ![The village at midday](media/day.png) | ![The village at night with lit windows](media/night.png) | ## What's in the repo | | | |---|---| | `SKILL.md`, `references/` | The skill: workflow, the rules that make the style work, and guides for style, motion, scenes, verification, matching a reference clip and rendering video. | | `lib/` | Four dependency-free TypeScript modules: drawing primitives (`ink.ts`), a walk/run solver (`gait.ts`), springs, pendulums and wind (`motion.ts`), and a time-of-day palette (`daynight.ts`). | | `examples/walker/` | One figure in about 150 lines: a man with a briefcase walks across the card; click him and he tips his hat. | | `examples/village/` | A full scene: a street of machiya, a tea house and a bath house by a canal, villagers on schedules, a cat, birds, a boatman, lit windows and reflections, about a dozen interactions. | | `scripts/` | Deterministic frame capture for video, and tools for measuring a reference clip. | ## Install the skill For Claude Code, clone it into your skills folder: ```sh git clone https://github.com/JDhruv14/line-art-animation ~/.claude/skills/line-art-animation ``` or into `.claude/skills/` inside a single project. Then ask for what you want, for example: - "Make a line art animation of a bakery at dawn: a baker carrying trays, steam from the oven, a cat in the window." - "Turn this clip into a looping line-art component, matching its walk exactly." (attach or link the clip) - "Add a day-night cycle to the scene and render a 30-second 1080p video." Claude reads `SKILL.md`, copies `lib/` into your project, shows one figure for approval before building the rest, and checks motion frame by frame before handing it over. ## Run the examples Requires Node 22.18 or newer. ```sh npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:5173 ``` In the village, drag the sun or moon across the sky to change the time, move the pointer

Style `@stickman-video-director` dan `line-art-animation` selesai di-port ke `style/` untuk engine **remotion** dan **fframes**. Folder root dibersihkan.

### 1. `style/stickman-video-director` (alias: `stickman`)
- **Visual DNA:** High-contrast stickman animation (stark black stage `#0a0a0f`, bold white strokes, red beanie `#ef4444`, yellow highlight `#facc15`).
- **Remotion Kit:** `<StickmanStage>`, `<StickFigure pose="stand|run|think|shock">`, `<SpeechBubble>`, `<StickmanBanner>`, `<StickmanCaptions>`.
- **fframes:** `tokens.rs`, `kit.rs`, `look.rs`, `video.rs`, `main.rs`, `Cargo.toml`.

### 2. `style/line-art-animation`
- **Visual DNA:** Hand-drawn ink on parchment (`#fbf8f1`), hairline pen strokes (1.5–2.5px), procedural walk solver, architectural Japanese/European line art, day-to-night transitions.
- **Remotion Kit:** `<ParchmentStage timeOfDay="day|dusk|night">`, `<LineArtWalker>`, `<LineArtHouse>`, `<LineArtBanner>`, `<LineArtCaptions>`, plus library modules (`gait.ts`, `ink.ts`, `motion.ts`, `daynight.ts`).
- **fframes:** `tokens.rs`, `kit.rs`, `look.rs`, `video.rs`, `main.rs`, `Cargo.toml`.

### Daftar Style Aktif (`motion_styles`):
```text
bang-motion
crosshatch
cut-paper
isometric
line-art-animation
math
papercut
pixel
riso
sketchbook
stickman
stickman-video-director
```

### Uji Scaffold:
```bash
./core/new_episode.sh <series_dir> 01-stickman Episode demo --style stickman-video-director --engine remotion
./core/new_episode.sh <series_dir> 01-lineart Episode demo --style line-art-animation --engine fframes
```
